Operations dashboard

Last updated 2026-08-02

Four reports, four links, and what to look at in each. This page holds no numbers of its own — every figure below lives in a tool that keeps it current, and a copy of it here would be wrong within a day while looking authoritative.

It is internal: nothing on the site links here, it is excluded from the index by the same allowlist that governs every other URL, and it is not in the sitemap.

The four reports

01

Search Console — Performance →

Impressions, clicks and average position for every query and every URL Google served, updated daily with about a two-day lag.

Set the date range to 28 days and sort PAGES by impressions: a page with impressions and no clicks has a title/description problem, a page with neither is not indexed yet — check it in the URL inspector before rewriting anything.

02

Analytics 4 — Realtime →

Property G-01Y1DJPFJ3. The last 30 minutes: page views as they happen, and events as they fire.

The only thing this view is for is proving the tag is alive after a deploy. Open a page, click a retailer link, and watch affiliate_click appear in the event count. If it does not, nothing below this line is measuring anything.

03

Analytics 4 — affiliate_click →

Admin → Data display → Events. affiliate_click is the one KEY EVENT this property has (starred 2026-08-02; purchase is Google's default and is not ours). Every exit sends it with three parameters: merchant, template, entity_id.

Compare the count against sessions for the same period — that ratio is the outbound click rate. Then split by template: a template converting far below the others is a layout problem, and a merchant converting far below the others is usually a price or a stock problem, not a copy one.

04

Latest price check

data-staging/price-check-2026-08-01.md — 29 registry links carrying a verified price, checked 2026-08-01. Read it in the workspace; it is not part of the published site.

Every price on the site degrades in the UI more than 14 days after its check date, so the question this file answers is which entities are about to go quiet. Run the job again before that happens rather than after.

PRD §9 — the four numbers, and where each one is

Impressions Search Console → Performance → Pages. Nothing in Analytics measures this; a page can have thousands of impressions and zero visits.
Clicks Search Console → Performance, the same table. This is clicks FROM Google, which is not the same number as Analytics sessions and will always be a little higher.
Outbound click rate Analytics → Events → affiliate_click count ÷ sessions for the same period. Enhanced measurement also records generic outbound clicks; ignore those here — they include internal navigation off-site and are not conversions.
Conversion by template Analytics → Events → affiliate_click, broken down by the "template" parameter (t1 / t2 / t3 / t4). Add "merchant" as a second dimension for the split PRD §8.7 asks for. Both parameters need registering once as custom dimensions in Admin → Custom definitions before they can be used as report breakdowns; until that is done they are visible on the event but not groupable.

One caveat worth keeping in front of you: every count above is ours, measured on this side of the click. There is no merchant-side report to reconcile it against, so an exit here means a reader left for a retailer and nothing more — not a sale, not a return, not a cancellation. Read the conversion numbers as direction, not as revenue, until something on the other side can be compared with them.

This page carries no retailer links, so there is no commission to disclose on it.
